q: How does a Ballari pellet plant work out CO2 per tonne of pellets?
title: Ballari pellet plants: CO2 per tonne
short: Add fuel burnt in the induration furnace or grate, such as coal, coke breeze, furnace oil or gas, to process CO2 from limestone and dolomite additives, then divide by tonnes of pellets. Pellets are covered by CBAM, and for them electricity is reported but not charged.
audience: Iron ore pellet plants in the Ballari and Hospet region of Karnataka

ul: Fuel: tonnes or kilolitres times the emission factor, using carbon content from supplier analysis where available.
Additives: tonnes of limestone or dolomite times 0.440 or 0.477 t CO2 per tonne of pure carbonate.
Bentonite and other binders without carbonates add no process CO2.

p: Grinding and balling use a lot of power. Record kWh at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for your footprint, even though CBAM does not charge it for iron and steel goods.
Buyers may want the figure per dry tonne. Keep the moisture basis of your production figure clear.
